England outside London is England minus London: the England row and the London row (pinned at region E12000007) are both bound, so this publisher partition member is derived rather than pinned; Chronicle stamps it at statistical_scope and test_uk_bus_targets asserts the partition reconciles to England within GBP 1,000.

BUS05i publishes no UK total and Microcosm declares no method to construct one.

BUS05i publishes no UK total and no England-to-UK uplift is declared. Net support binds instead as four country legs whose scopes differ: DfT BUS05bi net support (England, operators' view), Scottish Transport Statistics all government support (Scotland), StatsWales revenue outturn gross expenditure on concessionary fares and support to operators through local authorities only (Wales: no operator-side series and no Welsh Government grants outside the outturn), and the NITHC accounts' Public Service Obligation plus concessionary compensation as one bus-plus-rail cell excluding GBP 53.2m of other revenue funding (Northern Ireland). The legs are bound on their own terms; they are not a UK total under another name.

The OBR fuel duties fact is all-road-users receipts (freight, vans, business mileage) against a household frame; obr.fuel_duties_cars binds the cars receipts from the OBR vehicle-type release instead (ruling 2026-09-10). The all-road-users row is retained in the contract for registry parity and signed out here rather than carried as a calibration measure exclusion.

ONS Consumer Trends COICOP 04.5 (electricity, gas and other fuels) carries liquid and solid fuels the frame does not model; chronicle #271 (chronicle#270) published the 04.5.1 electricity and 04.5.2 gas sub-classes, which ons.household_electricity_expenditure and ons.household_gas_expenditure bind per fuel on the frame's own columns. The total row is retained in the contract for registry parity and signed out here (microcosm#890 F1).

HMRC Table 6's 15-and-below row (1,000 taxpayers, GBP 54m of gains, GBP 9m of tax in 2024-25) has no support: the CGT incidence clone and the size-band donors place gains on the oldest adult of a household, so the frame carries no gainer under 16 and the row would always measure zero. Signed out of the age-band fan-out; the eight adult bands stay bound.

Signed out; the twelve bands from 3,000 stay bound.

HMRC Table 4.1's individuals total row (61,000 claimants, GBP 18,443m of qualifying gains and GBP 1,821m of tax in 2024-25) is the sum of the eight published bands and carries no band edge, so it cannot be measured as a band row. Signed out of the band fan-out; the eight bands stay bound.

DWP's new State Pension £40.00 to under £60.00 a week cell (2,903 recipients over May to November 2025, 0.06% of new State Pension recipients) has no record on the frame: about thirty distinct new State Pension recipients report under £100 a week in FRS 2024-25, and the nearest of them restate above £60 at the 2025 rate the engine pays, so the row would always measure zero. Signed out of the weekly-amount fan-out; the other nine new State Pension bands stay bound.
